### American Integrity Insurance Group, Inc. Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results


November 10, 2026


***Growth accelerated with 41K voluntary new business policies sold in the third quarter, up 57% year-over-year, compared to 54% year-over-year growth in the second quarter of 2026***


***Record 83% growth in revenue in the third quarter year-over year***


***$39.6 million of income before income taxes, one of the most profitable quarters in our history***


***Gross premiums written grew 23% year-over-year to $293 million during the quarter***


***Net premiums earned of $101 million, up 95% year-over-year, nearly double the same period last year***


TAMPA, Fla.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


American Integrity Insurance Group, Inc. (“American Integrity,” “we,” “us,” “our” or the “Company”) (NYSE: AII), reported third quarter 2026 results.


Robert Ritchie, Chief Executive Officer, commented, “We delivered another strong quarter that reflects the continued execution of our strategy and the increasing strength of our voluntary growth platform. Following record voluntary new business production in the second quarter, we sustained that momentum in the third quarter, writing approximately 41,000 voluntary new business policies, an increase of 57% year over year, and an acceleration from the second quarter’s year-over-year growth rate. We are seeing broad-based growth across our key strategic initiatives and believe we have substantial runway ahead.”


Mr. Ritchie continued, “Our growth remains grounded in the disciplined underwriting and thoughtful risk selection that have defined American Integrity for more than two decades. As we approach the important milestone of half a million customers, it remains imperative that we remain focused on the same core principles that have made American Integrity successful through various market cycles.”


**Third Quarter 2026 Highlights:**


- Net income of $28.4 million, or $1.44 per diluted share. Adjusted net income 1 of $28.3 million, or $1.44 per diluted share
- Book value per share of $19.96, up 23.7% over September 30, 2025 and up 5.8% over June 30, 2026
- Return on equity of 29.8% and Adjusted return on equity 1 of 29.8%
- Policies in-force and in-force premium were 481,446 and $1,069 million, respectively, up 18.6% and 17.4%, respectively, over September 30, 2025
- Wrote 117,814 new and renewal policies in the voluntary market, an increase of 28.6% compared to the third quarter of 2025


- 8,003 voluntary new residential business policies in Tri-County region of Florida compared to 233 in the third quarter of 2025, a 34x increase
- 8,561 voluntary new business policies in our Florida middle-aged home category (excluding Tri-County) compared to 568 in the third quarter of 2025, a 15x increase
- Stable premium per policy year-over-year across our overall book


- Net premiums earned of $101.2 million, an increase of 94.5% compared to the third quarter of 2025
- Combined ratio of 70.6% compared to 78.9% in the third quarter of 2025
- Assumed no policies from Citizens Property Insurance Corporation (“Citizens”), as we determined that no policies from Citizens met our underwriting and targeted profitability standards


1 Adjusted net income, adjusted earnings per share and adjusted return on equity are non-GAAP financial measures. Please see the discussion below under the heading “Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures” for additional information concerning these and other non-GAAP financial measures.


**Third Quarter 2026 Commentary**


- Gross premiums written in the third quarter of 2026 increased by $54.2 million to $293.3 million from $239.1 million in the third quarter of 2025, primarily driven by growth in our voluntary market writings.
- Gross premiums earned in the third quarter of 2026 increased by $33.1 million to $255.0 million from $221.9 million in the third quarter of 2025.
- Ceded premiums earned in the third quarter of 2026 decreased by $16.1 million to $153.9 million compared to $170.0 million in the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to the reduction in our non-catastrophe quota share reinsurance arrangement.
- Net premiums earned in the third quarter of 2026 increased by $49.2 million to $101.2 million from $52.0 million in the third quarter of 2025.
- Net investment income in the third quarter of 2026 increased $1.5 million to $8.4 million compared to $6.9 million in the third quarter of 2025, primarily due to the increase in our invested assets driven by the increased in-force premiums.
- Losses and loss adjustment expenses (“LAE”) for the third quarter of 2026 increased $8.6 million to $38.3 million compared to $29.7 million for the third quarter of 2025. The loss and loss adjustment expenses ratio was 36.6% for the third quarter of 2026, compared to 54.1% for the third quarter of 2025. The net underlying loss and loss adjustment expense ratio 2 was 31.7% for the third quarter of 2026, down from 49.9% for the third quarter of 2025.
- Policy acquisition expenses and general and administrative expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were $18.0 million and $17.6 million, respectively, compared to $6.3 million and $7.3 million, respectively, in the third quarter of 2025. Period over period changes were due to new business production in the third quarter of 2026, the reduction in our non-catastrophe quota share reinsurance arrangement from 40% to 25% on January 1, 2026 and the benefit of Citizens take-outs in 2025.
- The expense ratio was 34.0% for the third quarter of 2026 compared to 24.8% for the third quarter of 2025. The combined ratio was 70.6% for the third quarter of 2026 compared to 78.9% for the third quarter of 2025.


2 Net underlying loss and loss adjustment expense ratio is a non-GAAP financial measure. Please see the discussion below under the heading “Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures” for additional information concerning this and other non-GAAP financial measures.

**Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Financial Measures:**


**Adjusted net income and adjusted earnings per share**


Adjusted net income is a non-GAAP financial measure defined as net income excluding net realized gains or losses on investments, stock compensation expense incurred in connection with our IPO, and certain non-recurring or non-cash expenses, including those incurred in connection with our IPO, net of tax. We use adjusted net income as an internal performance measure in the management of our operations because we believe it gives us and users of our financial information useful insight into our results of operations and our underlying business performance excluding the impact of realized gains and losses on the sale of securities, and one time items, which we do not view as core to the underlying trends in our business. Adjusted net income should not be viewed as a substitute for net income calculated in accordance with GAAP, and other companies may define adjusted net income differently.


Net income increased $15.2 million, or 115.4%, to $28.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $13.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Adjusted net income increased by $14.3 million, or 102.6%, to $28.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, from $14.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025.


Adjusted earnings per share is a non-GAAP measure, which is calculated as adjusted net income available to common shareholders divided by weighted average diluted common shares outstanding. Management believes this metric is meaningful, as it allows investors to evaluate underlying profitability and enhances comparability across periods by excluding items that are heavily impacted by investment market fluctuations and other economic factors and are not indicative of operating trends.

**Net underlying loss and loss adjustment expense ratio**


Net underlying loss and loss adjustment expense ratio is a non-GAAP measure. We calculate the net underlying loss and loss adjustment expense ratio by subtracting current year net catastrophe losses and prior year net reserve development from total net losses and LAE and dividing that amount by the sum of total net premiums earned plus policy fees. We use the net underlying loss and LAE ratio to allow us to analyze our loss trends before the impact of catastrophe losses and prior year reserve development. These two items can have a significant impact on our loss trends in a given period. We believe it is useful for investors to evaluate these components both separately and in the aggregate when reviewing our performance. The most directly comparable GAAP measure is the net loss and LAE ratio. The net underlying loss and LAE ratio should not be considered a substitute for the net loss and LAE ratio and does not reflect the overall profitability of our business.

**Gross underlying loss and loss adjustment expense ratio**


Gross underlying loss and loss adjustment expense ratio is a non-GAAP measure. We calculate the gross underlying loss and LAE ratio by adding net underlying loss and LAE and ceded non-catastrophe losses and dividing that amount by the sum of total gross premiums earned and policy fees. We use the gross underlying loss and LAE ratio to analyze our loss trends before the impact of reinsurance.


We believe it is useful for investors to evaluate the cost of non-catastrophe losses for every dollar of gross premiums earned. The most comparable GAAP measure is the net loss and LAE ratio. The gross underlying loss and LAE ratio should not be considered a substitute for net loss and LAE ratio and does not reflect the overall profitability of our business.

**About American Integrity Insurance Group, Inc.**


American Integrity Insurance Group, Inc. (NYSE: AII) is a leading provider of residential property insurance, focused on delivering innovative, reliable coverage to homeowners throughout the Southeast. Built on a foundation of integrity, resilience, and service, the Company’s mission is to be the most trusted and responsive insurance solution in the markets it serves. Founded in 2006 and headquartered in Tampa, American Integrity is committed to protecting policyholders with strength and purpose—today and for generations to come. For more information, visit[www.aii.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.aii.com&esheet=54638671&newsitemid=20261109354501&lan=en-US&anchor=www.aii.com&index=4&md5=105c1de20ecb61fcc923bcf63cd2ea68) .


**Forward-Looking Statements**


Certain statements in this press release and on the related teleconference call may be forward-looking statements.
